bibliography.abstract: Abstract The assessment of structural performance and service condition of high-speed railway (HSR) bridges is critical for meeting the lifecycle management requirements of HSR projects. To extract reliable structural information from bridge monitoring data, the identification of load-relevant parameters (e.g., train motion parameters) is essential. This paper proposes a method to identify load-relevant train motion parameters (i.e., number of carriages, direction of travel, traveling speed) during train crossing of HSR bridges, using structural strain monitoring data, with the dual goal of enabling accurate train load identification and supporting effective assessment of HSR bridge structural performance. An analytical model is established based on the dynamic strain response of the train-bridge interaction system during train passage. This model explicitly reveals the relationship between the waveform characteristics of structural strain time–history curves and the target train motion parameters. Building on this model, a set of algorithms for motion parameter identification is developed through systematic waveform analysis of structural strain monitoring data. The effectiveness and engineering applicability of the proposed method are validated using field monitoring data from an in-service HSR steel truss bridge. Results confirm that the identified parameters (number of carriages, travel direction, traveling speed) are consistent with the actual train operation status, verifying the method’s reliability for calibrating train load-related information and providing a practical tool for HSR bridge structural health monitoring.

en.caveats: The validation of the proposed method is demonstrated on a single in-service steel truss bridge, and its performance across different bridge types or structural materials is not detailed.
en.what: This study develops an analytical model and a set of waveform analysis algorithms to identify train motion parameters, including the number of carriages, direction of travel, and speed, using structural strain monitoring data from high-speed railway bridges. The method was validated using field monitoring data from an in-service high-speed railway steel truss bridge, successfully matching the identified parameters with actual train operations.
en.why: It provides a method to extract operational train characteristics directly from existing bridge strain sensors, enabling accurate train load identification and structural health monitoring without requiring dedicated trackside train-tracking hardware.
